# dsh-settings-resizable
**Resizable Settings dialog for DeepSeek Harness.** Drag any edge or corner of the Settings window,

drag the divider between the navigation column and the options, hit the arrow keys on a focused
hand
le, and the dialog keeps the sizes you chose the next time you open it.

A local DeepSeek Harness (DSH) client plugin that makes the Settings dialog resizable. It adds
eight

pointer handles to the edges and corners of the dialog plus one splitter between the
navigation col

umn and the options, lets the user drag them or press the arrow keys to change the
sizes, remembers

the chosen widths and height in `localStorage`, and clamps every size to the
viewport so the dialog

can never grow past the window. The plugin is a pure web-UI decoration: it
never replaces the applic

ation root, never appends a second application, and never relies on
build-hashed class names.
**Version:** 0.2.0 · **License:** MIT · **Host half:** intentionally empty (all behaviour is in `cli

## Screenshots
Default size on a 1408 × 797 viewport: 800 px wide, 749 px tall.
After dragging the right edge and the bottom edge, with the size persisted across a reload.
The navigation column dragged out to 308 px, with the options column reflowed beside it.
## Features

- Eight resize handles: north, south, east, west, and the four corners.
- A vertical divider between

the navigation column and the options: drag it, or focus it and press
the arrow keys, to change the

navigation width. The options column always keeps at least 320 px,
so the divider stops short of sq

ueezing the settings content.
- Pointer dragging with window-level tracking, so a drag keeps working

outside the dialog; a lost
`pointerup` (release outside the window, Alt-Tab) is detected on the nex

t pointer move and ends
the drag instead of leaving it alive.
- Keyboard resizing with the arrow key

s in 16 px steps on the focused handle or divider.
- Size persistence under a single versioned key,

`dsh-settings-resizable:v1`, as
`{width, height, navWidth}`.
- Minimum size of 480 × 400 px, with vi

ewport-derived maximums applied on every resize; the
navigation width is re-clamped whenever the dia

log changes size.
- Automatic handoff in the shell's fullscreen layout (narrow viewports, and the ti

tlebar/Electron
layout that never docks): the dialog stays fullscreen and the plugin removes its inl

ine styles,
handles, and divider.
- Accessible handles: each handle is a `role="separator"` with a l

ocalized `aria-label`, an
orientation attribute, and a visible focus ring. The plugin adds four tab

stops: the east, south,
and south-east handles (`tabindex="0"`), and the navigation divider. The oth

er five handles use
`tabindex="-1"` so the tab order does not stop eight times in a row. The edge ha

ndles also expose
an `aria-valuemin` / `aria-valuemax` / `aria-valuenow` triple that follows the cur

rent size and
limits; corners carry a position in their label instead. The divider carries the same

value triple
for the navigation width.
- Localized labels for Chinese, English, and Russian through

the DSH locale service, with a built-in
fallback. Both baseline locales (`zh` and `en`) are register

ed, which the service requires.
- Zero polling: a `MutationObserver` watches the document and re-att

aches the decoration when the
dialog is reopened.
- Full cleanup on close and on unload: listeners,

timers, handles, and the injected stylesheet are

## How it works
### Anchor attribute

The plugin locates the dialog through the stable attribute selector
`[data-shortcut-modal="settings"

]`. Build-hashed class names are never used as anchors, so a shell
[该节后续省略]
#### Why the width is inline

The injected rule selects `[data-shortcut-modal="settings"]`, which has the same specificity
(0,1,0)

as the shell's `.panel` column declaration, and the shell's stylesheet is inserted into
`<head>` af

ter ours. With equal specificity, document order decides: the rule loses, the column
stays at the sh

ell's `188px`, and only the custom property follows the drag. An inline declaration
outranks both, s

o `applyNavWidth()` writes the template inline — no `!important` is used, and the
rule is kept becau

se it is still correct wherever no later stylesheet shadows it.
`applyNavWidth()` repositions the di

vider after that write, so the divider lands on the real
column boundary.

The inline template is removed together with the control that can change it: in `removeSplitter()`
(

on close), in both mobile-handoff branches (`scan()` and `onResize()`), and in `dispose()`.
Otherwis

e a stale column would outlive the divider and outrank the shell's single-column
fullscreen layout.

The divider (`div.dsh-sr-handle.dsh-sr-split`, attribute `data-dsh-settings-resizable-split`) is a
6

px strip centered on the column boundary with `cursor: col-resize`, `touch-action: none`, and the
s

ame focus ring and fading grip as the edge handles. Its `top` and `height` come from the
navigation

cell's own rectangle, not from the panel: the navigation cell is the direct child of the
panel that

starts at the panel's left padding edge and reaches its bottom edge (the title cell sits
above it, s

o the bottom-left match is unambiguous). Injected nodes are skipped while matching,
because the sout

h-west handle sits on the same two edges. Its `left` is the cell's right edge
relative to the panel'
s padding box, the containing block of an absolutely positioned child.

If the navigation cell cannot be identified — an unexpected child order, or a shell that wraps its
c

hildren — the divider falls back to the applied column width with the panel's full inner height
inst
ead of disappearing; the next scan re-measures as soon as the cell is back.
Dragging the divider applies the pointer delta 1:1: the dialog's left edge does not move, so unlike

## Requirements

- DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 web UI or newer. The plugin was verified in a live DSH 0.2.2-rc.1 web host.
- A pro

file directory that DSH can install local plugin packages into.
- No runtime dependencies: the clien

t module is plain browser JavaScript loaded through
`window.__ModuleLoader__`.
